**Review of the search ad**

1. **"Plastic-Free Tea Bags" (headline):** Fine. Matches the allowlisted claim.

2. **"Our tea bags are plastic-free and home compostable."** Exact wording from the allowlist (supplier certificate, EN 13432). Fine.

3. **"Best tea I've ever had" - Emma, Leeds.** This is a problem on two counts:
   - It is a testimonial with no source in the policy. We have no record of Emma or her quote, so it has to be treated as invented. Invented testimonials are never allowed.
   - It carries a "best" superlative that we can't prove. Even a real customer quote would need to be checked and approved before being used in an ad, since it puts an unprovable superlative in our mouth.

**Suggested fix:** Remove the quote. If you want a second line, use an allowlisted claim instead, for example "Free UK delivery on orders over £25" or "Rated 4.8 out of 5 from over 1,200 reviews on our website."

Suggested rewrite:
Headline: Plastic-Free Tea Bags
Description: Our tea bags are plastic-free and home compostable. Free UK delivery on orders over £25.

Sam needs to approve the final version before it goes live, as with all public content.

```json
{"issues": [{"quote": "\"Best tea I've ever had\" - Emma, Leeds.", "type": "fake_testimonial"}, {"quote": "Best tea I've ever had", "type": "superlative"}], "publish": false}
```
